items.evidence: After a page.reload() the spec asserts statusInfo reads "Unfulfilled" and the fulfil button is enabled (fulfillment-cancel.spec.ts diff lines 79-81). That state comes from the server, so the test would fail if the cancel mutation never ran.
All three criteria are asserted: status "Unfulfilled" (line 74), fulfil action offered again (line 75), and still "Unfulfilled" after reload (lines 79-81).

Extends the existing OrderPage instead of adding a new class. It reuses dialog, timelineView, statusInfo, fulfillButton, findOrderId and ORDERS_SCENARIO. The new locators have no counterparts in OrderPage, AddressDialog or the other page objects.
No waitForTimeout or sleeps. cancelFulfillment waits on the dialog becoming hidden.
Imports test/expect from ../../fixtures/test.ts. No parallel() tag and no writes to the cache or dumps.

Every locator uses a data-test-id from the source (fulfillment-menu-button, cancel-fulfillment, cancel-fulfillment-select-field) or a role. The submit button and select field are scoped to the dialog. option.first() is allowed because the ticket accepts any warehouse.
Uses the scenario's existing "fulfilled" order through findOrderId. Nothing is created in the spec.
No hard-coded ids. The order is looked up by its scenario key, and the assertions use only status labels.
Uses the fixture's default admin session. No UI sign-in and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0 with no errors, and the spec is under e2e/tests/orders/.
Locators and the multi-step cancel flow are on OrderPage. The spec only calls cancelFulfillment and asserts on page-object locators.
The new members are readonly fields built from this.page / this.dialog (orderPage.ts diff lines 9-17), and the existing constructor(readonly page: Page) {} is unchanged.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (lines 64, 71).
One test for one story, with a test.step for cancelling and another for the reload.
The title states the behaviour and carries #e2e (line 63).
The header comment (lines 54-58) says what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first (toHaveText, toBeHidden, toBeEnabled).
Uses the imported ORDERS_SCENARIO and the "fulfilled" scenario key. The status literals match the suite's own practice, and no money is involved.
No cleanup hooks and no unique or random names.
No per-test timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep .ts, and test/expect come only from the fixture.
No any, casts or gql calls were added.
The only new comment is the cancelFulfillment JSDoc. It explains why the method switches to the timeline view and which warehouse it picks, so it gives reasons rather than narrating.

structured_output.summary: Submission bdb82dad passes all 23 checklist items (B1–B10, M1–M13). It adds OrderPage.cancelFulfillment with new locators on the existing page object, plus one spec. The spec starts from the orders scenario's fulfilled order, cancels the fulfillment, and checks that the status reads "Unfulfilled" and the fulfil button is offered again. It repeats both checks after a reload, which shows the server actually cancelled the fulfillment. The type check passes, and the spec follows the suite's fixture, step and locator conventions.
